page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.16-256 is a memory-dense virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at a 3.0 GHz clock speed, configured with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs through hyper-threading. System memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, providing an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic instructions such as AES and SHA-NI. The instance configuration includes no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, with network storage required for persistent filesystems.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high-tier memory subsystem capabilities paired with steady midrange compute performance. PassMark memory testing registers in the top 10 percent of tested systems with a score of 3005.02, supported by uncached large-block read throughput of 151.96 GB/sec and small-block cached read throughput of 1749.59 GB/sec. General multi-core processing falls in the middle tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 14819, a PassMark CPU score of 36717.62, and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 31767.47. While image processing and small-parameter language model generation perform strongly, large-model prompt processing shows diminished performance due to the lack of dedicated tensor acceleration hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high resource density for memory-bound workloads without incurring the expense of specialized GPU hardware. The absence of bundled local NVMe storage requires external block storage, representing an architectural dependency for disk I/O operations. This profile fits memory-centric services including in-memory datastores, distributed caching systems, extract-transform-load data pipelines, software compilation suites, and enterprise application backends.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.16-256 is a memory-focused virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at 3.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 physical cores, 32 dedicated vCPUs, and 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Benchmark results highlight a memory subsystem that ranks in the top 10 percent of tested configurations, achieving a 3005.02 PassMark memory score and 151.96 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth. Multithreaded compute throughput remains balanced, registering 14819 points in Geekbench multi-core testing. The instance includes no integrated GPU hardware and lacks bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent disk storage. This hardware composition delivers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy infrastructure, making it suited for in-memory caching layers, Redis deployments, enterprise databases, and data processing workloads.
